newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU threatens U.S. over textiles rules.
newsitem.headline: EU threatens U.S. over textiles rules.

text.p: The European Commission leapt to the defence of Europe's clothing industry Friday, threatening the United States with a trade complaint if it did not stop classifying Italian ties and the like as Asian.

It warned Washington that it would bring a complaint before the World Trade Organisation if it did not receive an offer soon to change rules it says harm European designers and clothing manufacturers.
At issue are U.S. rules of origin that the Commission says classify textile products such as Italian scarves, German furnishings or British cotton goods as being made elsewhere.

"America's origin rules say that even if a piece of grey cloth imported from China, India, Pakistan or elsewhere is cut, bleached, shrunk, dyed, printed or labelled in Europe, it does not benefit from EU origin," the Commission said in a statement.

"Even if the value added to the original cloth is 400 percent, and the product has been radically altered in Europe, it is still deemed to originate in the country where it was woven, and should bear the markings showing that origin," it said.
"These rules could harm top European designers and clothing manufacturers either by resulting in quotas or by undermining quality European labels as a selling point among American consumers."

The Commission, which is responsible for the 15-nation EU's trade policy, said it had investigated the situation using a new EU regulation under which individual companies can ask the Commission to probe an alleged barrier to exports.
"The European Commission has investigated and ... concluded that without a satisfactory offer from the United States soon, it will complain formally," it said.
